title: ALLWAYS — Cinema from the Rest of the Frame
subtitle: Twenty-four critic-protected passages across Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini Argon, OpenAI Sol, and Claude Sonnet

chapters.title: THE OCCASION & THE EDGE
chapters.quote:
A camera points at an event. More happens than the event can contain.
Someone waits for a doorway to clear. Someone moves a chair.

chapters.title: NEARMATCH
chapters.quote:
Two gestures can resemble one another and still belong to different lives.
We keep the pause that interrupts the alignment.

chapters.title: THE RELAY
chapters.quote:
The name joins always and all ways: recurrence through time,
and different routes through the same material.

chapters.title: THE WORK
chapters.quote:
Carrying, cleaning, preparing, repairing, waiting for access, making room.
We follow the activity that makes an event possible.

chapters.title: THE CARRIER & THE CHASE
chapters.quote:
An archive has already passed through many hands.
Our edit enters that work and becomes answerable for what it does next.

chapters.title: THE ROOM REMAINS
chapters.quote:
A moment does not have to explain a life to be worth keeping.
The room remains. That does not tell us everything about who left.
chapters.source: Between Takes · The Interval & The Room

shots.action: A boy crosses a fixed-camera domestic room, carries a chair to the window, and climbs onto it.
shots.nearmatch: Opening domestic threshold: recorded human action before computational erasure.
shots.why_chosen: Praised by the blind critic ('at 0:00-0:12 a boy crosses a fixed-camera room, carries a chair to the window, climbs on it'); establishes ALLWAYS's foundational proposition: someone moves a chair at the edge of the frame.

shots.source_title: Have I Told You Lately That I Love You?
shots.action: Three-panel inspection ledger: intact source pixels on the left, extracted person silhouette mask in the center, and Telea-inpainted empty armchair on the right.
shots.nearmatch: From Opus's occupied room to Argon's explicit disclosure of person-removal.
shots.why_chosen: Critic Tribunal 'Strength to preserve': 'The 3-panel inspection triptych layout (Original | Extracted Mask | Derived Empty Room)'. Keeps the mask and synthesized background separate from recorded pixels.

shots.action: A man and woman pause by an interior doorway as the official exchange ends and the post-action stillness takes over.
shots.nearmatch: Doorway geometry rhymes with the domestic rooms while shifting attention to the interval after speech.
shots.why_chosen: Cleared Sol's attention critic on V02 ('PASS from attention critic after specific 5s hold repair'): demonstrates holding a shot after the nominal action finishes.

shots.action: A toddler stands at a screen door, hand against the frame, staring directly back at the camera.
shots.nearmatch: From the adult doorway threshold in Sol 057 to a child's unguarded counter-gaze at the threshold.
shots.why_chosen: Explicitly singled out by Sonnet's independent critic ('Strength to protect: the toddler's backward stare at 14–17').

shots.action: A woman adjusts her collar and blouse at a desk, completing the self-preparatory gesture before settling into stillness.
shots.nearmatch: Initiates the NEARMATCH gesture chain: a complete collar adjustment with its pause intact.
shots.why_chosen: Verified cut-free single-shot window (max_diff < 16.0) fulfilling the ALMOST HUMAN opening requirement ('Begin with one complete collar adjustment, including the pause afterward').

shots.action: Split-screen pairing: on the left (1961), a man bends to arrange theatre chairs; on the right (1944), a woman adjusts and sits on a typing chair.
shots.nearmatch: Pairs two situated preparations across seventeen years without pretending they occurred simultaneously.
shots.why_chosen: Highlighted by Opus's blind critic ('Noticed before the brief: at 0:03-0:11 a man bends to arrange theatre chairs while a woman's hands tilt and then sit on a swivel chair').

shots.action: A subject exhales into a laboratory tube, raising the bell of a glass spirometer cylinder by the exact volume of his breath.
shots.nearmatch: Makes invisible human breath physically measurable before cutting to audible social breath (laughter).
shots.why_chosen: Earned a qualified VISUAL PASS in Sol's Round 2 ('The actual repair improves the mechanical demonstration substantively; no remaining visual objection').

shots.action: Three young women lean into one another as genuine, unscripted laughter spreads across their shoulders and faces.
shots.nearmatch: From solitary measured exhalation (Sol 063) to shared respiratory contagion across bodies.
shots.why_chosen: Praised by Sonnet's blind critic ('Strength to protect: the girls' sequence 25.2–31.2 is real shared in-source laughter with physical contagion—leaning, grabbing').

shots.action: Close-up of a young man lighting and drawing on a cigarette—activating the physical sense of the word 'draw'.
shots.nearmatch: Inaugurates the polysemic relay where a single word pivots across physical actions.
shots.why_chosen: Sonnet's critic passed 055-words and named this exact shot its anchor ('Strength to protect: the cigarette draw 13–22, the only shot where sound and the sense meet').

shots.action: Hands sort dividers inside an open wooden drawer while the soundtrack states: 'a place for everything and everything should be in its place.'
shots.nearmatch: Pivots from 'drawing' breath/smoke (Sonnet 055) to an open 'drawer' ordered by hand (Opus Homonym).
shots.why_chosen: Highlighted by Opus's blind critic ('Noticed before the brief: at 00:17.9-21.8 the voice says a place for everything... over hands sorting').

shots.source_title: Registered Circles (Globe, Moon Map, Signature Lens, Eye)
shots.action: Graphic constancy relay: a painted Earth globe, a magnifying lens over a moon map, a lens over a signature, and an eye behind glass hold the exact center rim.
shots.nearmatch: Shifts the relay from verbal polysemy (055) to pure geometric registration across four decades of film.
shots.why_chosen: Rated by Sonnet's blind critic as 'PASS (strongest proof in the batch) — Strength to protect: registration that holds through the opening'.

shots.action: A high diver traces a clean gravitational parabola across open sky from tower to water.
shots.nearmatch: Releases the centered static circle of 059 into a dynamic ballistic curve governed by gravity.
shots.why_chosen: Rated by Sonnet's blind critic as 'PASS (most complete realisation in the batch)'.

shots.action: A heavy yellow industrial tractor is hoisted by crane cables out over deep teal ocean water.
shots.nearmatch: Carries the suspended aerial arc of the diver (064) into suspended industrial tonnage and chromatic contrast.
shots.why_chosen: Explicitly protected by Sonnet's critic ('Strength to protect: Mixed-colour hinge at 7.5: a yellow engine swung out over teal sea. This hinge works.').

shots.action: A continuous ribbon of dark, viscous liquid pours into a white basin, expanding into a glossy concentric pool.
shots.nearmatch: From heavy mechanical suspension to fluid material affordance held for its full physical duration.
shots.why_chosen: Praised by Sonnet's critic ('Strength to protect: the 7.8 s pour 12.6–20.3 ... duration is earned').

shots.source_title: Care of the Hair and Nails
shots.action: Hands turn porcelain basin taps and wash carefully in running water to begin a composite morning.
shots.nearmatch: Fluid pouring into a circular white basin (061 Matter) rhymes directly with water running in a domestic porcelain sink.
shots.why_chosen: Passed Argon Round-2 Critic Tribunal: anchors the composite morning in a concrete, situated domestic task.

shots.action: A skilled machinist presses metal against a high-speed grinding wheel, sending a bright cascade of sparks across the workshop.
shots.nearmatch: Hands at the domestic basin (Argon 065) hand off to skilled industrial hands at the grinding wheel (Sol 065).
shots.why_chosen: Earned a qualified VISUAL PASS in Sol's Round 2 ('qualified VISUAL PASS for five differentiated archive practices').

shots.action: A weaver throws and beats a wooden handloom shuttle in a crisp, reciprocating horizontal rhythm.
shots.nearmatch: Matches rotary industrial craft (Sol 065) with reciprocating textile rhythm before releasing momentum outward.
shots.why_chosen: Passed Argon Round-2 Critic Tribunal: preserves the human craftsperson's bodily cadence inside repetitive work.

shots.action: After two withheld releases, the bowler's ball finally strikes the headpin and scatters all ten pins.
shots.nearmatch: Converts repetitive back-and-forth loom motion into forward release and physical impact.
shots.why_chosen: Explicitly protected by Opus's blind critic ('Protect: the bowler return and the pin-fall payoff at 12-13').

shots.action: A lone figure sprints across a wide open heath under nitrate-era sky, carrying directional momentum across landscapes.
shots.nearmatch: Transfers the kinetic impact of Split Second into open-air human pursuit across a horizon line.
shots.why_chosen: Passed Argon Round-2 Critic Tribunal: clean horizon line and unbroken directional run.

shots.action: A dense flock of birds wheels across the sky above a horizontal row of silhouetted figures standing along a ridge.
shots.nearmatch: Graphic horizon match with the lone runner on the heath (Argon 19), expanding one runner into a collective horizon and sky.
shots.why_chosen: Passed Sol's visual critic ('bounded VISUAL PASS — Deliberately spaced human placements beside a linear guide contrast with nonlinear flock motion').
shots.critic_verdict: PASS · Linear human row vs. flock (Sol)

shots.action: An archivist's hands hold and inspect a 16mm metal film reel and celluloid strip—the physical carrier behind every image.
shots.nearmatch: Returns from the sky to the physical 16mm spool that carried all twenty preceding fragments.
shots.why_chosen: Passed Sol's Round 2 critic ('bounded VISUAL PASS for the truthful parent/selection/reduced-derivative relation').

shots.action: The voiceover recalls an 'untouched kitchen' (plant, red chair, icebox)—until two visitors in coats step into frame behind a museum rope stanchion, quietly exposing the borrowed memory.
shots.nearmatch: The emotional centerpiece of ALLWAYS: picture and museum rope break the narrator's claim of private memory without a single didactic caption.
shots.why_chosen: The ONLY film in Opus 5.5's run to pass its blind critic ('VERDICT: pass, narrowly. Protect: the kitchen sequence at 23-40s. The narration lists details that match the frames, and the exhibit rope then breaks the claim without any comment.').

shots.action: Close-up of an archival clock dial as the sweep hand marks the shared minute across disparate lives.
shots.nearmatch: Marks the time elapsed in the museum kitchen before opening the door to the final empty room.
shots.why_chosen: Passed Argon Round-2 Critic Tribunal: anchors the horological montage in a legible, unadorned timepiece.

shots.action: Seen through an open white door: an unoccupied chair, a small table with a telephone, and a lit lamp held in stillness after everyone has left.
shots.nearmatch: Completes the circle begun in Cut 01: the chair by the window gives way to the empty chair and lit lamp after the occasion is over.
shots.why_chosen: Explicitly protected by Sonnet's blind critic ('Strength to protect: the empty-room hold at 46.25–48.5') and embodies Between Takes: 'The room remains. That does not tell us everything about who left.'
